definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: 2002 defines 'character' in four senses (§2002:4, 4.26 to 4.29: coded value, graphic character in a screen item, COBOL character, code value in storage) and 'coded character set' (4.40); 2023's clause 3 defines none of them and uses the words in their ordinary sense. GR15 positions the screen in 'alphanumeric character positions' (4.31). Screen ACCEPT is processor-dependent in 2002 (§2002:3.1.5, B.3), and the compiler refuses it at --std 2002 (COBOL1560/COBOL1707, the reader's screen1.cob), so the evidence is unaffected. The term picks out the same characters in both, so the scope and the evidence do not change.
